note: The second survey. Every question here sets a field the ranking engine already reads, so an answer changes the order of the course list immediately. Nothing measures personality — that is what the first survey is for, and this one must never imply it fell short.

questions.sub: Money and family matter more here than ambition. Answer for the life you actually have.

options.text: Near home — I'd stay and commute
I'd move, but only to certain cities
Anywhere in Italy, if the course is right

questions.prompt: How long a journey could you do every day?

options.text: Up to two hours, if it's worth it

questions.prompt: What kind of place would suit you?
questions.sub: Where you live for three years shapes the three years as much as the course does.

options.text: A big city — more going on, more expensive
A small place where I'd know people

questions.prompt: What could your family manage each month?
questions.sub: Rent, food and transport — not fees. There's no wrong answer and nobody sees this.

options.text: Under €400 — it has to be cheap

questions.prompt: Do you know your family's ISEE band?
questions.sub: It decides your fees by law. Below €22,000 most public courses cost nothing.

questions.prompt: How much maths can you live with?
questions.sub: Be honest rather than brave. This is the single most common reason people abandon a course.

options.text: Bring it on — I'm good at it

questions.prompt: Are you open to a two-year professional course?
questions.sub: An ITS is shorter and more hands-on than a degree, and leads straight to work.

options.text: ITS only — I want to work sooner

questions.sub: Private institutions can cost several thousand a year.
